title: Directional exemplar annealing – prompt experiments & failure notes
content:
Purpose:
- Brain-dump / scratchpad for a small set of experiments where I try “directional exemplar annealing": gradually changing few-shot exemplars from close distribution to far distribution to see model calibration and hallucination behavior.
- Goal: obtain robust few-shot templates that degrade gracefully when user inputs drift (domain shift).

Notes on concept:
- Annealing idea: present a sequence of exemplars that shift a target attribute (tone, verbosity, factuality style) across the prompt such that later exemplars are progressively less similar to the input. Hypothesis: model will learn the intended transformation but remain tolerant to drift, and fallback behavior becomes smoother.
- Compare against static exemplar sets and random-mix sets. Also compare ordering: ordered (close->far), reversed (far->close), interleaved.

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Models: local-dev-davinci-like (quantized test), hosted-small, hosted-medium (redwood catalog aliases used in notes).
- Temperatures: 0.0, 0.2, 0.6, 1.0
- Prompt lengths: 3-shot vs 6-shot vs 0-shot
- Metrics tracked: exact-match on structured outputs, token-level hallucination count (manual), BLEU-ish for paraphrase tasks, human-judged factuality (small sample).

Working templates (examples) – aim: rewrite customer email into concise bullet summary with action items
- Instruction top (fixed):
  You are an assistant that converts raw emails into concise, neutral bullet summaries with explicit action items. Keep each action as a separate line starting with "ACTION:" and include a one-line context at top.

- Annealing exemplar set (3-shot, close->far):
  EX1 (close) – input: long email with explicit ask, output: context + 3 ACTION lines, uses exact phrases from email.
  EX2 (middle) – input: semi-formal email, output: context + 2 ACTION lines, condenses and normalizes names.
  EX3 (far) – input: short casual note missing explicit ask, output: context + suggested ACTION with a confirmation step.

Examples to paste into prompt (literal few-shot):

Input (EX1):
"Hi team, we need the Q3 numbers by Friday. Priya please send the workbook, and Jordan loop in finance if any gaps. Also schedule a 30m sync if open questions remain."
Output (EX1):
"Context: Request for Q3 numbers and clarification on gaps.
ACTION: Priya -> send Q3 workbook to the team by Friday.
ACTION: Jordan -> contact finance to identify and resolve any gaps.
ACTION: Team -> schedule 30-minute sync if questions remain."

Input (EX3):
"Can we get the numbers soon? Might need a quick check."
Output (EX3):
"Context: Implicit request for numbers; uncertainty about who owns the action.
ACTION: Confirm owner and deadline for delivering the numbers.
ACTION: If owner unknown -> suggest Priya or Jordan as point of contact."

Observed failure patterns during early runs:
- Repetition: at higher temps (0.8+), model repeated the ACTION label or duplicated lines (same action phrased differently).
- Hallucinated owners: model invented people when none were mentioned (e.g., "assign to Alex"), particularly with far exemplars interleaved.
- Over-confident confirmations: for inputs missing dates, model filled plausible dates instead of asking for confirmation when tempo>0.2.

Mitigations tried and results:
- Add a small guard clause in instruction: "If the input lacks explicit owner or deadline, output a confirmation action rather than inventing one." Reduces hallucinated owners by ~70% in manual check at temp=0.2.
- Use temperature 0.0 for structured, critical outputs (e.g., legal/finance) — preserves terseness but less tolerant of paraphrase variety.
- Explicit token budget note: "Keep output <= 120 tokens" helped reduce duplication.
- Ordering: close->far ordering performed better (fewer hallucinations) than far->close in 3/4 manual comparisons. Hypothesis: starting with high-fidelity exemplars anchors the model.

New experiment ideas (todo):
- Annealing with embedding-similarity gating: dynamically choose next exemplar by similarity vs input and enforce anneal schedule.
- Try soft-anchoring: include a short example of "what to do when data missing" between exemplars to reduce confabulation.
- Evaluate across model variants with KV-cache effects — long contexts + annealing might push cache eviction patterns and change behavior.

Failure case catalogue (short):
- FC-001 (Made-up owner): invented owner when none present. Conditions: high temp, far-first ordering. Workaround: confirmation action requirement.
- FC-002 (Date hallucination): model names a concrete due date. Conditions: short input with one-off scheduling words. Workaround: explicit "do not guess dates" instruction.
- FC-003 (Action duplication): same action phrased in two lines. Conditions: long exemplar list + temperature>0.6. Workaround: dedup heuristic in post-processing or instruct single-line actions only.

Small set of few-shot templates for other target tasks (quick list):
- SQL-from-natural-language (3-shot anneal): start with perfect aligned examples, then include slightly ambiguous phrasing, then include negative example showing "ambiguous -> ask clarifying Q".
- Tone-transfer (formalize): exemplars move from identical content to paraphrase with different formality scales.
- Safety-probe: include a poisoned exemplar at the end to test whether annealing reduces or amplifies instruction-following of harmful content. (Ethics check: do inside test harness.)

Implementation notes / PRD sketch (for later):
- CLI: script to build annealed prompt sequences from an exemplar database, with options for ordering, anneal-rate, and gating by semantic-similarity threshold.
- Logging: store exemplar indices in request metadata so post-hoc analysis can link outputs to which exemplars produced hallucinations.
- Small eval harness: sample 200 user inputs artificially drifted from training distribution and score for hallucination, action correctness, and need-for-clarification.

Quick todo (me):
- [ ] run batch at temp=0.2 and 0.0 for hosted-medium with 3 orders (close->far, far->close, interleaved) on the email->actions task (50 inputs each).
- [ ] add explicit negative exemplars (ambiguous -> ask question) into the anneal set.
- [ ] write small script to auto-dedup ACTION lines and run as postprocess to measure how much of duplication is model vs my pipeline.
- [ ] surface promising exemplars to the shared prompt playbook repo (PR stub exists).

Notes to self: keep language minimal in instruction header. Models latch on to long prefatory prose in unexpected ways. When in doubt, prefer a one-line directive plus the exemplars.

Random capture of a short failing prompt (raw):
- Prompt used: "Summarize and list actions. Use ACTION:"
- Output: two identical ACTION lines and an extra invented owner.
- Immediate fix used: appended "If you do not know who owns an action, write ACTION: [CONFIRM OWNER]" and reran; improvement seen.

References and cross-links:
- Related user scratchpad: seed-cascade-experiments-journal (local stash) — similar idea but different annealing schedule.
- Link to internal scratch PR: see linked_artifacts above.

End notes: writing down informal failure patterns helps — will iterate with Jordan on gating heuristics next week.
